en_alt: Complete this exercise at home.
note: "Complete" tracks выполнить more closely than the bare "Do" and should also be accepted by the word-bank drill.

en_alt: Tomorrow he will complete all the assignments.
note: зада́ние is glossed "assignment", so that rendering should also be accepted.

ru: Е́сли бы я обеща́л, я бы вы́полнил рабо́ту.
en: If I had promised, I would have carried out the work.
note: The English mixes a past counterfactual protasis ("had promised") with a present-unreal apodosis; the perfective бы+past reads as a single completed event, so "would have carried out".

ru: На но́вой рабо́те я бу́ду выполня́ть ва́жные зада́чи.
en_alt: At the new job I will be carrying out important tasks.
note: «На работе» is equally "at work / at the job"; both prepositions should be accepted.

en_alt: The dog obeys commands.
note: Idiomatic English for the same sentence; the literal "carries out" stays as en_gb.

en_alt: They fulfilled the plan every month.
note: The imperfective past also renders as a plain past with the "every month" adverbial carrying the habituality.

en_alt: Are you doing your work?
note: Russian present imperfective covers both habitual and progressive readings here.

ru: Без интере́са я бы выполня́ла рабо́ту ме́дленно.
Без разреше́ния я бы не выпуска́л соба́ку.

en_alt: The publishing house published magazines.
note: «выпускать журналы» of a publisher is ordinarily "published"; the existing "used to release" stays as en_gb.

ru: С весны́ заво́д бу́дет выпуска́ть но́вую моде́ль.

en_alt: I will let the bird go free.
note: "Set free" is fine, but the more literal "let go free" for вы́пустить на свобо́ду should also be accepted.

ru: Е́сли бы пти́ца попа́лась, я бы её вы́пустил.
note: Present-unreal on both sides and a single completed release; consistent.

ru: Без слов я бы выража́л чу́вства жеста́ми.
В письме́ я бу́ду выража́ть свои́ мы́сли я́сно.
en: In the letter I will be expressing my thoughts clearly.
note: бу́ду + imperfective is the corpus's "will be V-ing" frame; the flat "will express" collides with all three perfective вы́разить futures.
Frame-only collision with вы́разил/вы́разила, but the subject and object differ completely, so the contrast drill still has a cue; "Her face was expressing joy" would be worse English.

en: She expressed her gratitude with a word.
note: "in a word" in English means "to sum up"; «сло́вом» here is the instrumental means, and благода́рность is glossed "gratitude".

ru: Е́сли бы спроси́ли, я бы вы́разила своё мне́ние.

note: Collision resolved on the imperfective side (бу́ду выража́ть → "will be expressing"); the perfective future is correct as it stands.
Same collision, fixed on the imperfective side.

en_alt: Prices will go up by winter.
note: The "rise" sense of вы́расти is outside the headword gloss "to grow up" but is the only natural English for prices.

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло бо́льше со́лнца, цветы́ бы вы́росли вы́ше.
Че́рез год де́рево вы́растет до кры́ши.
en_alt: In a year the tree will grow as high as the roof.
note: "grow up to the roof" is ambiguous between the phrasal verb and the preposition; the alt disambiguates and also separates this from the расти frame.

en_alt: She tore a page out of the notepad.
note: листо́к of a notepad is equally "page" in English.

ru: Е́сли бы лист был испо́рчен, я бы его́ вы́рвал.
en_alt: If the sheet were spoiled, I would tear it out.
note: лист is glossed "leaf / sheet"; the sibling sentence already uses "sheet".
Russian leaves the possessor of «из рук» implicit; English requires one, so "my hands" is unavoidable rather than added detail.

ru: Си́льный ве́тер вы́рвет зо́нтик из рук.

en_alt: I will say everything that I think.
note: The relative pronoun may be kept explicit; both should be accepted.

en_alt: He expressed his opinion directly.
note: Matches the headword gloss "to express" alongside the existing "stated".

ru: Е́сли бы спроси́ли, я бы вы́сказал всё пря́мо.
За́втра на собра́нии она́ вы́скажет своё мне́ние.

en_alt: She expressed her doubts.
note: Gloss-matching alternative to "voiced".

en_alt: Will you express your doubts?
note: Gloss-matching alternative to "voice".

ru: Е́сли бы зазвони́л звоно́к, я бы вы́скочил из кла́сса.

en_alt: The cat jumped out from under the table.
note: The gloss-literal "jumped out" should be accepted alongside "darted out".

ru: Он вы́скочил на у́лицу без ша́пки.
Я вы́скочу из ваго́на на ста́нции.
На остано́вке я вы́скочу из авто́буса пе́рвым.

en_alt: The doctor listened to the patient's complaints.
note: "Heard out … complaints" is stiff; the natural rendering should also be accepted.

ru: Е́сли бы у меня́ бы́ло вре́мя, я бы тебя́ вы́слушала.

en_alt: Listen to me carefully.
note: "Hear me out carefully" is odd English — "hear out" does not normally take a manner adverb; the alt is what a native would say.

en_alt: I will listen to your opinion.
note: "Hear out" idiomatically takes a person, not an opinion; the alt is the natural rendering.

en: The museum will put new paintings on display.
note: A museum does not "put out" paintings; the sibling sentence about the gallery already uses the right English for the same verb.

en_alt: We will put the goods out in the window.
note: Gloss-literal alternative to "display".

ru: Е́сли бы пого́да была́ тёплой, я бы вы́ставил цветы́ на балко́н.
За́втра арти́ст бу́дет выступа́ть на большо́й сце́не.
en_alt: Tomorrow the artist will be performing on the big stage.
note: арти́ст is "artist/performer" and выступа́ть is glossed "to perform"; both wordings should be accepted.
выступа́ть at a conference is "to speak"; a sense the gloss "to perform" does not cover, but the English is right.

en: They were performing in front of the audience.
note: Bare "performed" collides with the perfective «Певи́ца вы́ступила блестя́ще»; the imperfective past is the side that should carry the ongoing reading.

ru: Без подгото́вки я бы выступа́ла пло́хо.

en_alt: He delivered a report.
note: «вы́ступить с до́кладом» is a fixed frame; the alt keeps до́клад "report" visible for the learner.

ru: За́втра он вы́ступит с ва́жным заявле́нием.
Е́сли бы меня́ пригласи́ли, я бы вы́ступила с пе́сней.
en_alt: If they invited me, I would perform a song.
note: The impersonal plural «пригласи́ли» also renders actively as "if they invited me".
Correct English for the perfective; the collision is fixed on the imperfective side.

en_alt: She pulled the wallet out of the bag.
note: кошелёк is glossed "wallet", and the Russian does not say whose bag.

ru: Ско́ро рыба́к вы́тащит сеть из воды́.
Е́сли бы ло́дка засе́ла, мы бы её вы́тащили.
По́сле до́лгой доро́ги я с удово́льствием вы́тяну но́ги.
en_alt: After the long journey I will stretch out my legs with pleasure.
note: «с удово́льствием» renders literally as "with pleasure" as well as "gladly".

en_alt: I will stretch out my hand in front of me.
note: ру́ка is glossed "hand"; both readings of the sentence are valid.

ru: Е́сли бы уста́л, я бы вы́тянул но́ги на дива́не.

en_alt: Get out of the bus here.
note: "Get off the bus" is the right English; the literal alt keeps «из» visible for the learner.

ru: Он выхо́дит из до́ма ка́ждое у́тро.
note: The flagged frame overlap with вы́шла is only the particle "out"; tense and subject differ, so the drill retains its cue.

ru: Я выхожу́ из до́ма в во́семь.
en_alt: I go out of the house at eight.
note: "Leave the house" drops «из»; the literal version should also be accepted.

ru: Они́ выходи́ли на прогу́лку ка́ждый ве́чер.
С за́втрашнего дня я бу́ду выходи́ть на пробе́жку.
Ты выхо́дишь из до́ма ка́ждое у́тро?
Без зо́нта я бы не выходи́ла в дождь.
note: "Would not go out" is the correct habitual reading for the imperfective; the partner вы́шел sentence is the side that could take "would have gone out", and it is not in this packet.

en_alt: Find out who the boss is here.
note: Both renderings of «кто здесь гла́вный» are natural.

en_alt: Will you find out the reason for the mistake?
note: причи́на is glossed "reason".

en_alt: I will find out the reason for the mistake.
note: причи́на is glossed "reason".

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло вре́мя, я бы вы́яснил пра́вду.

en_alt: The truth will soon become clear.
note: "Come to light" is idiomatic; the plainer alt tracks вы́ясниться more directly.

ru: Е́сли бы прове́рили докуме́нты, всё бы вы́яснилось.

en_alt: Soon it will become clear who was right.
note: "It will turn out who…" is marginal English; the alt is what a native would write, while en_gb keeps the gloss visible.

ru: Я гляжу́ в окно́ на у́лицу.
Без очко́в я бы гляде́л на доро́гу с трудо́м.
note: "Would look" is right for the imperfective; the flagged partner (поглядеть) differs entirely in content, so the frame overlap leaves a usable cue.

en_alt: She was looking at the stars.
note: гляде́ть is glossed "to look"; the plain verb should be accepted alongside "gazing".

en_alt: Are you looking at the stars?
note: Same as its past-tense sibling: the gloss-literal "looking" should be accepted.

ru: Ве́чером я бу́ду гляде́ть на звёзды с балко́на.
Она́ бы гля́нула на отчёт, но забы́ла очки́.
en_alt: She would have glanced at the report, but she forgot her glasses.
note: "Would have looked" correctly marks the perfective; the alt uses the headword gloss "to glance".

en_alt: I will glance in the mirror.
note: Gloss-literal alternative to "take a quick look".
"Take a look at who has come" is not how this is said in English; «Глянь, кто пришёл!» is "Look who has come!".

ru: По тако́й доро́ге я бы не гнал.
note: "Drive so fast" is not added detail — speed is part of what гнать means, which the bare gloss "to drive" does not convey.

en_alt: The wind drove the clouds to the east.
note: «на восто́к» renders equally as "to the east".

en_alt: Don't drive the car so quickly!
note: бы́стро is glossed "quickly".

ru: У́тром пасту́х бу́дет гнать ста́до на луг.
В де́тстве он говори́л о́чень ти́хо.
en_alt: In childhood he spoke very quietly.
note: «В де́тстве» maps literally onto "in childhood" as well as "as a child".

en_alt: I do not remember the person who was speaking.
note: челове́к is glossed "person" and carries no gender here.

en_alt: He speaks too quickly.
note: бы́стро is glossed "quickly".

ru: Ско́ро я бу́ду говори́ть по-ру́сски свобо́дно.

en_alt: The letter spoke about the weather.
note: «о» renders as "about" as readily as "of".

ru: Как говори́тся, лу́чше по́здно, чем никогда́.
В отчёте бу́дет говори́ться о результа́тах.
Е́сли бы так говори́лось, я бы пове́рила.
В э́тих кни́гах говоря́тся ра́зные ве́щи.
note: говори́ться is normally impersonal — «В э́тих кни́гах говори́тся о ра́зных веща́х» / «говори́тся ра́зное»; the personal plural «говоря́тся ра́зные ве́щи» reads oddly, but the sentence is the word's only plural example so a human should decide.
